title: Partner shelf launch brief + landing copy drafts
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the working brief for a partner shelf launch (cloud marketplaces + partner co-sell shelf). It bundles the minimum technical/legal gates with short-form listing copy and a concise asset matrix that product marketing and the partner success team can use to speed up marketplace publication across AWS/Azure/GCP and selected ISV portals.

TL;DR (for execs):
- Goal: Get partner offer live across three marketplaces within a 6-week sprint.
- Primary customer: Platform engineering + ML infra teams at growth SaaS/enterprise buyers.
- Must-haves to start: 2-sentence landing, 50-word one-liner, 600-word overview, 1 hero image, security compliance badge (SOC2 or ISO), pricing SKU mapping.

Audience & positioning notes:
- Buyer persona: SRE/Platform lead wanting predictable inference at scale; cares about latency SLOs, predictable cost, and deployment flexibility (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Value prop focus: "Bring predictable, production-grade LLM inference to your stack with clear unit economics and ops-grade controls." Avoid deep research claims — emphasize integration, SLAs, and observability.

Minimum publication gates (technical/legal):
- Legal & commercial: signed partner agreement (POA or reseller), billing entity name, tax id or VAT where applicable, support contact + escalation matrix.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 or SOC2-in-progress note; customer data handling blurb; optional KMS/HSM support line.
- Offering metadata: offer name (<= 80 chars), short description (<= 140 chars), long description (<= 600 words), tags (LLM, inference, GPU, dedicated, private), logo (PNG/SVG, 1:1, 1200px), hero image (16:9, 1920x1080).
- Technical: deployment options list (hosted API, dedicated capacity, private VPC), compatible regions, minimum throughput profile examples (tokens/sec at 99th percentile), model variants supported, quantization/instance family notes.
- Billing/SKU: price units (per-token or flat throughput band), mapping to marketplace SKU strings, trial credits amount and activation process.
- Test artifact: working sandbox integration (API key limited to test endpoints) and simple CloudFormation / ARM / Terraform quickstart for customers (reference template link).

Marketplace-specific divergences (quick guidance):
- AWS Marketplace: emphasize AMI/CloudFormation quickstart for Dedicated; require AWS Marketplace Metering SKU and legal entity contact. Provide 1-line usage example using aws sdk.
- Azure Marketplace: highlight private plan availability and Azure AD integration notes. Include ARM template + AAD app registration guidance.
- GCP Marketplace: provide container-based quickstart for private deployment and billing mapping to GCP billing account.

Short-form copy matrix (variants to use across listing tiles, email subject lines, and paid ads):
1) One-liners (<= 140 chars):
- "Redwood Inference — predictable, production LLM inference with dedicated capacity and private deployments."
- "Serve LLMs with low latency, transparent costs, and enterprise controls — hosted, dedicated, or on-prem."
- "Turnkey LLM inference: SLAs, cost controls, and operations tooling for production apps."

2) 50-word summary (marketing tile):
- "Redwood Inference provides production-grade LLM serving across hosted APIs, reserved GPU capacity, and private deployments. Deliver consistent latency and cost controls with observability, model versioning, and automated fallbacks — all through a single API and marketplace-friendly deployment options."

3) 150–300 word overview (long description draft — for listing detail pages):
- "Productionizing large language models is more than raw performance — it’s predictable economics, operational controls, and secure deployment. Redwood Inference unifies a GPU-optimized serving runtime with orchestration and observability so engineering teams can ship LLM features reliably. Choose hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated reserved capacity for steady throughput, or Private deployment for VPC/on-prem compliance. Built-in caching, batching, and model fallback policies reduce token costs while preserving quality. Instrumentation includes token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency dashboards, and eval-based regression alerts. Integrates with customer KMS, SSO, and supports canary and A/B rollouts for model updates."

Feature bullets (short) for marketplace tiles:
- Turnkey hosting + private deployments
- SLA-backed Dedicated capacity options
- Token-level cost and latency analytics
- Autoscaling + burst for predictable throughput
- KV/prefix caching and batching to lower per-token costs
- Model rollouts, canaries, and auto-fallbacks

Call-to-action variants:
- "Get started with free trial credits"
- "Request a demo and throughput consult"
- "Start a 14-day sandbox — deploy in minutes"

Required assets checklist (publisher intake form fields + notes):
- Company legal name (string) — REQUIRED
- Primary technical contact name/email — REQUIRED
- Marketplace legal contact (for contract) — REQUIRED
- Short description (<=140 chars) — REQUIRED
- Long description (<=600 words) — REQUIRED
- Hero image (16:9) and 3 thumbnails (square) — REQUIRED
- Logos: color & white on transparent (SVG + PNG) — REQUIRED
- Customer-facing PDF: "How Redwood inference integrates" (1–2 pages) — RECOMMENDED
- Quickstart templates: CFN / TF / ARM / k8s manifest — REQUIRED for Dedicated/Private offerings
- Test API key + sandbox endpoint + sample dataset — REQUIRED
- Compliance badges or statement (SOC2 / ISO) — REQUIRED if available
- Pricing table & SKU mapping document (CSV) — REQUIRED

Co-marketing copy snippets (partner-ready) — short email + social post variants:
- Email subject: "Integrate Redwood Inference — predictable LLM serving for your customers"
- Email body (short): "We’re launching a partner-ready offer on [Marketplace]. Redwood Inference provides a single API to run LLMs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with SLAs and cost controls. Set up a sandbox or request a demo."
- Social post: "Now on [Marketplace]: Redwood Inference — production-ready LLM serving across hosted, dedicated & private deployments. Try the sandbox: [link]"

Launch timeline (6-week sprint template):
- Week 0: Kickoff (legal sign-off, designate partner PMs) — owners: Partner Sales + Legal
- Week 1: Asset completion (copy, images, quickstart templates) — owners: PM + PMM + Solutions Eng
- Week 2: Technical intake (sandbox endpoint + billing SKU mapping) — owners: Solutions Eng + Platform Eng
- Week 3: Marketplace submission & publisher QA — owners: Partner Ops + PMM
- Week 4: Publisher feedback remediation & compliance checks — owners: Eng + Legal
- Week 5: Final approval + co-marketing plan & assets — owners: Partner Marketing
- Week 6: Go-live + announcement cadence — owners: Growth + Customer Success

Open questions / risk log (working):
- Trial activation flow: Who provisions trial credits in marketplace vs Redwood console? (ACTION: @Evan)
- Pricing model: per-token vs throughput band — need finance sign-off for SKU mapping (ACTION: @Priya)
- Support SLAs across marketplace purchases: do we route through marketplace or maintain direct support? (ACTION: Partner Sales)
- Private deployment licensing: confirm whether marketplace listing can reference a separate enterprise contract (ACTION: Legal)

Next steps (this sprint):
- Finalize the 50-word and 600-word descriptions and provide to publisher intake by EOD Friday. (Owner: Ayesha)
- Solutions Eng to upload CFN + TF quickstarts to the assets repo and attach a sample test key (Owner: Jamal).
- PMM to prepare two co-marketing email templates and 1 social card (Owner: Marisol).

Appendix: sample copy snippets for easy paste (multi-channel)
- Headline: "High-performance LLM inference, production-ready."
- Subhead: "Scale inference with predictable latency, cost, and enterprise controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 2-sentence elevator: "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams run LLMs in production with transparent unit economics, observability, and deployment choices. Faster time-to-value with the controls teams need to operate reliably at scale."

References and templates:
- Confluence: product listing style guide (link above)
- GitHub: marketplace-assets repo (link above)
- Jira: JIRA-PLAT-812 (publisher intake board)

Notes (author):
- Keep technical metrics (latency/cost) conservative in copy — prefer linking to a benchmarks page vs listing numbers on the vendor listing to avoid repeated publisher rejections.
- This doc is intentionally concise; hand off long-form collateral (whitepaper + integration guide) to the Solutions Eng docs folder after asset freeze.
